diagnosis: Customer on legacy_auth (business tier, us-west) is asking what the move to Unified Auth involves and whether it can be rolled back. KB kb-0012 covers the migration steps and states that rollback is not possible once legacy tokens are disabled. Question-type request; no escalation per policy.
reply: Thanks for planning ahead on the move to Unified Auth. Migration replaces your account-wide token with scoped keys, and we recommend a dual-running window: create the scoped keys, cut your traffic over to them, and only then disable the legacy token. One important note on rollback: once the legacy token is disabled, the migration cannot be reversed, so we suggest validating the scoped keys fully during the dual-running window before disabling the legacy token. Happy to help you plan the cutover steps if you have questions.
